steps: Excess pressure in a soap bubble is given by P = 4T/R.
End 1 has a hemispherical bubble of radius r, so P1 = 4T/r.
End 2 has a sub-hemispherical bubble, meaning its radius of curvature R2 > r.
Excess pressure at end 2 is P2 = 4T/R2, which implies P2 < P1.
Air flows from higher pressure to lower pressure, so air flows from end 1 to end 2.
As air leaves end 1, the volume of the bubble at end 1 decreases.
